title: Ashura: gratitude and grief
hook: the fast of Musa, and the memory of Husayn
tomorrow: Auntie's hosting a mawlid. Dad isn't going. who's right?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a fresh year: a direction, not a countdown. Early in that first month comes a day that holds two memories at once.

A cold bottle of water, handed to you on a hot day by a stranger, for nothing. On Ashura, in some Muslim neighborhoods, that happens on purpose: tables of water and juice by the road, free to anyone passing. And in other homes on the same day, people are fasting, no water at all until sunset. One gives water away; one goes without it. Same day. How?
screen: `A COLD BOTTLE, FOR NOTHING.` → `WATER BY THE ROAD.` → `NO WATER UNTIL SUNSET.` → `SAME DAY. HOW?`

segments.voice: Ashura holds two memories. The first is a rescue. In Sahih al-Bukhari, when the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came to Medina, he found Jews fasting this day. They told him it was the day God saved Musa and the Children of Israel from their enemy, and Musa had fasted it in thanks. He answered that he, too, stood close to Musa, and he fasted it and told people to fast. In a later report in Sahih Muslim, he said that if he lived to the next year he would fast the ninth as well, so some fast two days. Another report in Muslim says the Ashura fast wipes away the year before. The second memory is a grief. On Ashura, al-Tabari's history records, Husayn, the Prophet's grandson, was killed at Karbala with members of his family, after they'd been cut off from the river's water. Shia Muslims mourn him on this day, with gatherings, recitations and tears, and some set out water for strangers, remembering his thirst. In Sunni practice, the day's sunna is the fast for Musa's rescue, and Husayn is honored too. Some Muslims hold both. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: a sip of water can be a memorial. So the day's sense is water, withheld in gratitude and given away in grief. That's rescue and grief.
screen: `A RESCUE: MUSA'S FAST.` · `THE NINTH AS WELL.` · `A GRIEF: HUSAYN AT KARBALA.` · `WATER WITHHELD, WATER GIVEN.` · then, large: `RESCUE AND GRIEF.`

segments.voice: Pour a glass of water, or hold the one you have. Notice its weight, its coolness, the small sound it makes. Take one slow sip and let it rest on your tongue before you swallow; if you're fasting, just hold the glass. Then set it down and stay with the two memories: a people rescued, a family left thirsty.
screen: `ONE GLASS.` · `ONE SLOW SIP.` · `A RESCUE. A THIRST.`

segments.voice: Ashura: a day early in Muharram, kept with a fast for Musa's rescue and in mourning for Husayn, the Prophet's grandson.
Hold this one gently: rescue and grief can share a day, and one glass of water can carry both. Four days into this part.

screen: `DAY 1691 COUNTS.` → `THE MONTHLY AND YEARLY RHYTHM · 4 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: AUNTIE'S MAWLID, AND DAD ISN'T GOING.`

howItsDone: On Ashura, Sunni Muslims who keep the sunna fast the day, some adding the day before; Shia Muslims hold mourning gatherings (majalis) for Husayn and some set up stalls offering free water and drinks to passersby.

chat.meaning: Bukhari's report ties the fast to God saving Musa; al-Tabari records Husayn's death at Karbala on Ashura. Some Muslims hold both.

Ashura.meaning: a day in Muharram of fasting and of mourning

Husayn.meaning: the Prophet's grandson, killed at Karbala

Karbala.meaning: the place in Iraq where Husayn was killed

al-Tabari.meaning: an early historian whose history records Karbala

Shia.meaning: Muslims who follow the imams of the Prophet's family

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2004 (the Jews of Medina fasting Ashura, the day God saved Musa and the Children of Israel; he fasted it and ordered it)
Sahih Muslim 1134 (if I live to next year, I will fast the ninth)
Sahih Muslim 1162 (the Ashura fast expiates the year before)
al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk (the death of Husayn at Karbala on Ashura; the water of the river cut off)
sources.work: al-Tabari, History of the Prophets and Kings

notes: For parents: the lesson mentions Husayn's death at Karbala in one gentle line (killed with members of his family, after being cut off from water); no violent detail is told.

Bukhari 2004 says 'we have more right to Musa than you'; the script renders it as 'he, too, stood close to Musa' to avoid a contrast with the Jews of Medina. A Keeper should confirm this is fair to the report.
Sunni and Shia practice described side by side, neither ranked; 'In Sunni practice, the day's sunna is the fast': confirm phrasing with Keepers of both.
The day's date in Muharram is deliberately not stated (only 'early in Muharram' and 'the ninth as well').
